newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HUSSAIN AND THORPE PLUNDER AUSTRALIAN ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HUSSAIN AND THORPE PLUNDER AUSTRALIAN ATTACK.

text.p: England batsmen Nasser Hussain and Graham Thorpe plundered a weakened Australian attack on Friday to achieve the highest score of their respective test careers on the second day of the first Ashes test at Edgbaston.
At lunch, England were 335 for three in reply to Australia's first innings 118 with Hussain on 158 not out and Thorpe on 135.

Australia's need of at least one replacement bowler was emphasised by the morning's events. Jason Gillespie stayed off the field having treatment for a strained hamstring and Greg Blewett was unable to bowl either because of a knee injury.
Coach Geoff Marsh had said on Thursday that he was likely to request a replacement, with Paul Reiffel and Adam Dale the two contenders.

To make matters worse, Shane Warne, Michael Bevan and Steve Waugh were all guilty of loose bowling. Warne was driven out of the attack after conceding 23 runs in four overs, during which Thorpe reached his third century in four England matches.
It came up with his 14th four, from 164 balls, to follow hundreds in the first and second tests against New Zealand in February.
Hussain, having survived a close lbw appeal off Glenn McGrath, reached three figures off his 189th ball, with 17 fours.
The other milestone was a new record fourth-wicket partnership for England against Australia, beating the 222 by Wally Hammond and Eddie Paynter in 1938.

In their different ways, the two batsmen were equally severe on bad balls, of which there was no shortage. It was accordingly it was all the more surprising that paceman Mike Kasprowicz was not brought on until shortly before lunch, when the new ball was taken.
